items.title: Sepang Vision Lab
items.summary: Race-intelligence lab for Sepang International Circuit: circuit geometry, simulated telemetry, replay, weather scenarios and Monte Carlo strategy.

items.title: QualityPlus
items.summary: Data quality management turned into a product: scored checks, a remediation-to-publish workflow for trusted data, and AI assistance at three points.
items.problem: Oil & gas datasets arrive incomplete, duplicated and inconsistent, and fixing them happens in spreadsheets with no audit trail.
items.outcome: Proof of concept demonstrated at SPE AI Summit.

items.title: Duplicate Question Detection (NLP)
items.summary: Master's research: FastText embeddings plus PCA to detect duplicate questions on 404k Quora pairs, keeping 83.68% accuracy while cutting training time by two thirds and memory by 83%.
items.problem: Q&A platforms fill up with duplicate questions, and the accurate deep-learning detectors are too heavy to run at scale.
items.outcome: 83.68% accuracy at 200 dimensions, 0.33% below the full 1,200-dimension baseline, with 66.7% faster training and 83.4% less memory.
items.learning: The most useful result was the trade-off curve, not the top accuracy: most of the meaning survives aggressive compression.

items.title: LeadSightz
items.summary: Cursor × Anthropic Hackathon 2025: sales automation with Claude for intelligent lead management and insights.
items.problem: Prospect research, qualification and outreach take sales teams hours per lead. The hackathon brief was to automate that loop with AI.
items.outcome: Built in a weekend at the Cursor × Anthropic Hackathon MY 2025 (Monash University Malaysia, 6 and 7 December 2025) and deployed on Vercel. The team was a Top 20 nominee.
items.learning: Scope is the real constraint in a hackathon: a narrow, working flow with Claude at its centre beat a wide set of half-built features.
highlights: Smart lead discovery: AI-assisted prospect identification
Automated qualification: Claude analyses and scores each lead
Personalised outreach messages generated at scale
Analytics dashboard for performance and conversion
Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind, with Claude Sonnet 4.5 through the Anthropic API

items.title: EduGen
items.summary: AI-powered SPM question generator for Malaysian students.
items.problem: SPM students need a lot of practice questions across many subjects, matched to the chapters they are actually studying.
items.outcome: A live web app that generates 40 objective questions per quiz for seven SPM subjects, with explanations and a study dashboard.
items.learning: Generation is the easy part. Constraining it to the syllabus, the right form level and a clear difficulty is what makes AI-generated questions useful.
highlights: Seven subjects: Mathematics, Additional Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Pendidikan Islam and Sejarah
Form 4 and Form 5 content, chosen chapter by chapter
Easy, medium and hard questions, each with a detailed explanation
Study dashboard: quiz history, average scores, strong and weak chapters
Questions generated with the Google Gemini API

items.title: Job Matching System T2
items.summary: XGBoost-powered job matching with semantic analysis for accurate candidate–job matching.
items.problem: An existing job-matching flow used hardcoded rules presented as a decision tree: rigid, redundant, and unable to explain its scores.
items.outcome: A proof of concept on Streamlit that replaces the rules with an XGBoost model and explains every score, with a written architecture review of the old flow.
items.learning: Explainability is a feature. SHAP values made the model easier to trust than the hand-written rules it replaced.
highlights: XGBoost model trained on historical matches in place of hardcoded scoring
Feature engineering: semantic skill similarity, experience relative to requirements, education hierarchy, certification relevance
SHAP explanations showing which factors drove each score
Redesigned flow that computes features once and reuses them
Documented limitations: training data needs, cold start for new job categories

items.title: Face Recognition System
items.summary: OpenCV face recognition with a Streamlit interface, HOG feature extraction and SVM classification.
items.problem: Build a face detection and recognition web app that is light enough to deploy without heavy dependencies such as dlib.
items.outcome: A Streamlit app that detects, aligns and recognises faces from uploads or the camera, and reports accuracy, precision, recall and F1.
items.learning: Classic computer vision still goes a long way: good detection and alignment mattered as much as the classifier.
highlights: Face detection with OpenCV’s DNN detector, falling back to Haar cascades
Face alignment using eye detection
Recognition with HOG features and an SVM classifier, trained on the LFW dataset
Data augmentation: flips, rotations and brightness changes
Model evaluation metrics shown in the app

items.title: HR Analytics & Attrition Model
items.summary: Predict employee attrition with ML models and an interactive dashboard for retention insights.
items.problem: Organisations want to know which employees are at risk of leaving, and why, before it happens.
items.outcome: A live Streamlit dashboard on the IBM HR Analytics Attrition dataset that explores attrition drivers and predicts attrition risk.
items.learning: The most useful output was not the prediction but the drivers: overtime, work-life balance and career growth explained more than salary did.
highlights: Exploratory analysis of department-level attrition trends
Feature engineering, scaling and encoding
Multiple models compared, including Logistic Regression and Random Forest
Interactive dashboard for exploring the data and getting predictions
Findings: overtime raises quit rates; work-life balance often matters more than salary; growth opportunities reduce turnover

items.title: Aircraft Journey Summary Extractor
items.summary: Turns photos of aircraft journey summary forms, including handwriting, into structured JSON using Gemini’s vision model.
items.problem: Journey summary forms are partly handwritten and full of aviation abbreviations, which traditional OCR reads poorly.
items.outcome: A single-step extractor that returns validated JSON (aircraft, registration, route, crew, fuel, load, defect message) in about two to three seconds per form.
items.learning: Domain context in the prompt was the biggest lever: telling the model it is a maintenance technician and listing abbreviations lifted handwriting accuracy from about 60% to about 95%.
highlights: Gemini 2.0 Flash vision chosen over OCR plus NLP, AWS Textract and GPT-4 Vision, with the trade-offs documented
Prompt with aviation expertise and abbreviations (FWD, GND, A/C, DD, MEL)
JSON validation: required fields, integer types, clean-up of model output
Graceful batch processing: one bad form does not block the rest
Estimated cost of about $0.001 per form

items.title: Job Matching System T1
items.summary: Modular job matching with quantitative scoring on skills, experience and education.
items.problem: Candidate-job scoring logic was hard to maintain and debug, and could not be extended or fed with new data easily.
items.outcome: A modular Streamlit proof of concept that scores candidate-job fit from weighted skills, experience, education and certifications.
items.learning: Separating configuration, scoring and UI made the system easier to reason about, and it set up the ML version that followed (T2).
highlights: Weights and thresholds in a YAML configuration, not in code
Scoring service separated from data loading and visualisation
Dashboard with adjustable weights and a per-component score breakdown
Custom application input and JSON upload with validation
Export of results to JSON and CSV

items.title: Plant Disease Classification
items.summary: Transfer learning with CNNs to classify plant diseases from leaf images.
items.problem: Compare building an image classifier from scratch with transfer learning, and measure the difference properly rather than from a single run.
items.outcome: VGG16 transfer learning reached 68.11% average validation accuracy against 48.07% for a custom CNN, across five training runs each.
items.learning: Both models overfit (about 99% training accuracy), which made the case for regularisation and more varied data as clearly as the headline comparison.
highlights: Custom CNN: three convolution blocks with batch normalisation and a dense head
VGG16 pre-trained on ImageNet, frozen, with a new classification head
Five separate training phases per model for reliable averages
Training and validation accuracy and loss recorded for every phase

items.title: London Bike Sharing Analysis
items.summary: Cleaning and preparing the London bike-sharing dataset in Python so it is ready for reliable analysis.
items.problem: Raw public datasets arrive with duplicates, inconsistent types and formats, and missing values.
items.outcome: A cleaned, validated dataset and a notebook documenting every transformation.
items.learning: Writing down each cleaning decision matters as much as the code: it is what makes the analysis reproducible.
highlights: Dataset pulled directly from Kaggle and extracted with Python
Duplicates removed and data types standardised with pandas
Dates and strings standardised
Validation checks for consistency and integrity

items.title: Power BI Apocalypse Food Prep
items.summary: Power BI dashboard for food-preparation planning with resource tracking.
items.problem: Turn a planning dataset kept in Excel into something people can explore and act on.
items.outcome: An interactive Power BI dashboard built on data prepared in Excel.
items.learning: Modelling the relationships between tables up front is what makes filters and drill-downs work naturally later.
highlights: Data prepared in Excel and transformed with Power Query
Data model with relationships between tables
Slicers, filters and drill-downs for exploration
Consistent formatting, tooltips and navigation

items.title: Excel Bike Sales Dashboard
items.summary: Cleaning a raw bike sales dataset in Excel so it is ready for analysis.
items.problem: The raw sales data had errors, duplicates, inconsistent formats and missing values.
items.outcome: A clean, validated dataset with before-and-after versions published in the repository.
items.learning: Most analysis time is spent before the first chart. Clean data makes every later step faster and more trustworthy.
highlights: Cleaning functions: TRIM, CLEAN, IFERROR, ISNUMBER, TEXT
Cross-checks with lookup formulas (VLOOKUP, INDEX and MATCH)
Duplicates removed and missing values handled
Validation rules to prevent future entry errors

items.title: Excel Coffee Sales Dashboard
items.summary: Coffee sales trends and customer segmentation in an interactive Excel dashboard.
items.problem: Sales data is hard to read in rows; decision-makers need the trends at a glance.
items.outcome: An interactive Excel dashboard of coffee orders that a beginner can filter and explore.
items.learning: A well-designed spreadsheet dashboard can answer most day-to-day questions before a BI tool is needed.
highlights: Pivot tables and pivot charts for summaries
Slicers and drop-downs for interactive filtering
Conditional formatting to highlight key figures
Documentation for updating the data

items.title: Balang
items.summary: A Malaysian probability party game: read the jar of 25 kuih tokens, bet on secret prediction cards, and play friends in peer-to-peer rooms with no backend.
items.problem: Party games about probability are usually either pure luck or pure maths. I wanted one that is easy to learn in a round, social with friends, and still rewards reading the odds, without running a server.
items.outcome: A playable multiplayer game at balang.madebyrazeen.com: rooms by code, link or QR, three-round matches, bots that fill empty seats, and a shareable result card.
items.learning: Keeping the engine as plain, tested TypeScript separate from the UI makes balance testing possible: bots can play whole matches with no UI and report how the rewards behave.
highlights: Game engine as a pure state machine: 25 tokens of five kuih, a secret draw order, 12 prediction card types
Rewards priced from each card’s probability at deal time using Monte Carlo simulation
Peer-to-peer rooms over WebRTC (PeerJS): the host’s browser is the authority and guests only receive their own view
Bots take over a player’s turns if they disconnect, until they reconnect
Discard phases, a final negative card and KAW-KAW (double the value or lose it) for risk management

items.title: VSB
items.summary: A Malaysian social-volleyball platform where organizers create sessions and players discover games, see who is playing, book places and take part in a community.
items.problem: Coordinating social volleyball sessions through WhatsApp and individual messages is unnecessarily difficult.
highlights: Session discovery
Booking
Players
Community
Player identity

items.title: FORMA
items.summary: A visual data workbench that makes the path from messy input to a reliable pipeline easier to see, work with and reproduce, while keeping engineering control.
items.problem: Data engineering repeatedly requires inspecting, selecting, cleaning, transforming, validating, running and reviewing data through workflows that are often fragmented across code and tools.
highlights: Core loop: see, select, transform, verify, run, export
Pipeline stages: source, select, extract, clean, transform, validate, load
Pipelines shown step by step on a canvas
Exceptions go to a review queue instead of being lost
Exports readable Python that produces the same output
items.tagline: Shape messy data into reliable pipelines.

items.title: AEM Movie Night
items.summary: A small booking system built for an office movie-night activity.
items.problem: Turning a small manual coordination problem into a usable system.
